title: An immersive multisensory virtual reality approach to the study of human-built environment interactions
research_question: To develop a novel method for studying human-built environment interaction under multimodal (visual, auditory and thermal) conditions using virtual reality technology, and to apply this method to understand end-users' response to a semi-outdoor environment involving visual, thermal, and auditory stimuli.

participants.description: Participants for a within-subject experiment with two MIVE scenarios. Specific demographics not provided in this paper, referred to Lyu et al. (2022).

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Multisensory Immersive Virtual Environment (MIVE) simulating a semi-outdoor environment (SkyPark, Melbourne CBD, Australia). Visuals included detailed 3D models of buildings, greenery, animated objects, realistic material shaders, and atmospheric conditions (sunlight, daylight, wind cues like falling leaves, grass/tree movement). Auditory stimuli included ambient traffic noise, bird songs (Magpie, Golden Whistler), pedestrian crossing signals, tram bells, and breeze rustling tree leaves, rendered binaurally using HRTFs. Thermal stimuli included ambient air temperature (28°C, 60% RH) delivered by constant air volume AC, direct solar radiation simulated by 10 quartz tungsten halogen lamps (250W each) achieving mean radiant temperatures (Tmrt) between 35.0-39.6°C, and wind simulated by bladeless fans achieving 0.95 m/s. Two scenarios were presented: 'sunlight only' and 'sunlight + shade' (offering adaptive opportunity to move between sun and shade).

mechanisms: Congruent sensory cues are processed more fluently, leading to higher preference and improved presence in VR.
Immersion and interaction with the virtual environment provide a sense of Presence by making the subject feel physically present and behave accordingly.
Dynamic interaction between users and multiple sensory components enables comprehensive data collection and holistic understanding of human-environment interaction.
Affordability and feasibility of VR methodology compared to traditional field studies.
implementation_implications: Can be used as an empirical research tool in environmental psychology, architectural science, and technology.
Can serve as a preoccupancy evaluation tool for built environmental practices.
Can be used as a stakeholder engagement tool for sustainable project initiatives.
Facilitates collaboration between environmental consultants, engineers, landscape architects, and architects by integrating building performance simulation results into an experiential virtual space.

Cost summary of the multisensory VR system, detailing devices for visual/auditory and thermal simulation and their quantities and costs.

limitations: Heat lamps and fans were used for convective and radiative heat transfer; conductive thermal apparatus should be considered in future research.
Humidity could be added to MIVE simulation with HVAC systems or local humidifier devices.

No benchmark between the actual environment and the virtual environment was provided; validation studies comparing multi-sensory perceptions, perceived presence, and behaviors between actual and MIVE exposure are needed.
Calibration of auditory playback in relation to actual recording using a head and torso simulator wearing the VR headset is needed.
The sense of smell, identified as important for holistic experience, deserves further exploration and integration into VR.
Users' perceived realism for the three visual environmental layers (immediate, contextual, atmospheric) needs to be assessed and benchmarked.
